reviewer: Codex, user-designated technical and synthetic-data realism reviewer
review_scope: Identity, demographic, workforce and source-context plausibility; no licensed clinical or vendor certification claimed
sampling: Deterministic stratification across all five age bands, four administrative-sex values, six self-report categories, seven language/unknown states, changed/unchanged histories, eight worker roles, three employers, three employment types, later hires and former staff.

findings.observations: Reviewed all 100 patient rows. Cohort-appropriate names, middle names/initials, hyphenation, suffix and age variation are plausible; no indexed generic names. Rare cross-series names and unknown administrative attributes are retained rather than guessed from a name.

Constructed street/apartment addresses vary across the three declared Illinois city/postal areas. Automated full-cohort checks separately verify reserved .example email and 555-01xx contacts; addresses are fictional combinations, not copied addresses or a deliverability claim.

Self-report is generated independently before probabilistic surname selection. Census aggregate weights with cross-population mixing improve plausibility without imputing a person category from a name. Disease generation is independently tested against surname changes.

Reviewed all 50 worker rows, including physicians, nursing, therapy, laboratory/imaging, pharmacy, environmental and administrative staff; employer, credential, FTE, agency/contract cost premiums, hires and terminations form plausible demonstration records.

Full-data validators, not a visual name review, establish referential integrity and effective/known history boundaries. Opening problem/allergy assertions consume the frozen condition budget. Clinical journeys and outcomes remain later work.

limitations: Configured catchment and cost/coverage assumptions are fictional rather than US benchmarks.
No real identities, license registries, live Workday/Axiom extracts or patient records were used.
This review approves only the matching identity sample and master-data implementation; full healthcare data acceptance remains blocked.
additional_review_notes: Re-reviewed all 150 identities after documented SSA registration-label curation and canonical ordering of configuration distributions.

The sample now includes Jayne Brenda Andress, Glenn Peters, Lois Williams and Mathew Justin Castillo with distinct adult histories; the reviewed worker roles/types and contractual costs remain coherent.
Cross-series/unisex names and cross-population surnames are configured probabilistic cases; administrative self-report is retained rather than overwritten from appearance of a name.
